name: Gristle
description: Gristle is a notorious goblin mercenary who operates out of the Thornwaste badlands. Most goblins travel in packs, but Gristle works alone — partly by choice, partly because nobody can stand him for long. He's earned a reputation for taking impossible contracts and surviving through sheer stubbornness and a mechanical hookshot arm that replaced the one he lost in circumstances he refuses to discuss. Tavern rumors claim he once held a bridge alone against a dozen hobgoblin soldiers, though Gristle himself just scowls when asked about it.

legendsAndLore.text: Gristle is a goblin mercenary known for his mechanical hookshot prosthesis and foul temper.
He's an expert ambusher who coats his weapons in a potent spider-derived poison. He never takes jobs involving children or animals — everything else is fair game.
Gristle was once part of a goblin warband called the Rust Fang Company. He's the sole survivor of a job gone wrong, and the hookshot arm is a reminder of what he lost.

encounters.description: Gristle operates in wilderness areas, particularly rocky terrain where his hookshot gives him an advantage.

groups.creatures: Signs of Gristle's passage (old campsites, hookshot marks on cliff faces)
groups.treasure: a discarded poison vial (empty) and 3 (1d6) cp
a vial of spider venom (3 doses), 28 (4d12) gp, and a tattered map of local bounties

groups.creatures: Gristle with 2 to 4 hired goblin scouts
groups.treasure: a +1 scimitar, a potion of climbing, and 55 (10d10) gp

signs.text: Deep hookshot gouges in a rock face or tree trunk
The faint smell of spider venom on the wind
A small campfire, still warm — only one bedroll
A dead bounty target, neatly dispatched with a single blade wound
Grumbling and cursing in Goblin from somewhere above you

behavior.text: Watching from a high vantage point, hookshot ready
Counting coins and muttering about being underpaid
Sharpening his scimitar with an annoyed expression
Eating dried meat alone and glaring at anyone who approaches
Negotiating a contract — poorly, because he has no patience for haggling
Swinging between cliff faces with his hookshot, scouting the area
Tending to his mechanical arm with careful, practiced movements
Picking a fight with someone twice his size

names: Gristle doesn't use aliases. If you hear the name, it's already too late to run.
